correctness.rationale: Map invariance makes the x- and y-marginals identical. Applying invariance to the second coordinate gives the exact cubic moment law E[x^3]=(a-b-1)E[x]. On a nonnegative support, Cauchy-Schwarz yields E[x^2]^2<=E[x]E[x^3], hence Var(x)<=m(rho-m) and m<=rho. The Cauchy-Schwarz equality condition forces x to take only 0 and rho; equal marginals and forward invariance eliminate the two off-diagonal support points, leaving exactly mixtures of the two fixed atoms. Odd symmetry proves the third-quadrant statement, and the periodic-orbit side-visiting result follows by summing x(x^2-rho^2) over a period. The packaged checker verifies the invariant-moment algebra, fixed-point relation, sharp mixture formulas, and the exact pre-crisis rho-squared value.

value.rationale: The Holmes map is a classical low-dimensional model of Duffing Poincare dynamics, and the published pre-crisis regime is organized by two symmetry-related chaotic attractors confined to opposite quadrants. The accepted theorem attaches an exact statistical geometry to those natural branches: the fixed-point amplitude rho is a hard mean bound and generates a sharp variance parabola, with equality completely classified by fixed-point mixtures. Thus any computed one-sided periodic or chaotic invariant state must lie strictly inside a parameter-explicit moment region, providing a simple exact diagnostic tied directly to the attractor-merger setting rather than an arbitrary moment calculation.
